title: ActProbe: Action-Space Probe for Early Failure Detection of Generative Robot Policies
action_head: mixed: discrete action tokens (OpenVLA) and flow/diffusion action experts (pi0, pi0.5, GR00T)
methods: action-only failure probe on two signals from a single forward pass: temporal consistency error between consecutive action chunks and action chunk magnitude
question: Are emitted action chunks alone enough for early failure detection, without white-box access to policy internals?
key_findings: Early-detection ROC-AUC at 25% of the episode averages 75.8% across nine splits, 4.6 points above the strongest white-box baseline SAFE-MLP and 9.0 points above it on unseen tasks.
On seen tasks, hidden-state probes stay competitive in this limited-data regime; the action-only probe matches them.
Internal-feature probes overfit seen tasks; the action-space probe generalizes better to unseen tasks.
A probe trained on GR00T in RoboCasa simulation transfers zero-shot to the same policy on a Unitree G1 humanoid for two pick tasks.

benchmarks: two real pick tasks on a Unitree G1
evidence.scale: 50 training episodes per task; ablations averaged over 3 seeds
evidence.baselines: SAFE-LSTM, SAFE-MLP and TDQC variants, cosine k-NN on hidden states, STAC and other resampling or observation detectors

closed_loop: Online detection during closed-loop rollouts; no intervention on the policy.
critique: Important counterpoint for the internals-based monitoring literature: if output-only signals match or beat hidden-state probes, especially on unseen tasks, then a monitor's success is not evidence that the internals carry special failure information.
Same 50-episode training budget for all detectors favors low-dimensional inputs; hidden-state probes might close the gap with more data.
one_line: Two scalar signals from the emitted action chunks predict failure as well as or better than hidden-state probes like SAFE, especially on unseen tasks, which questions how much internal access buys for failure monitoring.
